## Annotation

Haw gives a developmental account of accessible housing and support services in British Columbia from the early 1970s through the late 1980s (Paraplegic Lodge 1972; first group home 1974; Long Term Care and hour-pooling 1978; Kelly Court 1979). For this archive, the material Creekview passages are:

1. Creekview 202 opened in **September 1985** as “an integrated self managed independent living project developed by CPA and at least 6 former residents of Pearson Hospital, five of whom were ventilator-dependent,” occupying the equivalent of six one-bedroom apartments (4,700 square feet) in a 100-unit CMHC-funded co-operative.
2. The Ministry of Health and the Workers Compensation Board “have provided funding to the tenants through CPA for purchase of support services such as a paramedic, home-maker, nursing, physiotherapy and occupational therapy.” Attendants were trained by Pearson staff. All six men “are equal members of the co-op”; Haw says one is president of the building and involved in hiring and firing staff.
3. “In 1987 an independent evaluation of Creekview 202 was published which confirmed the success of the project in three respects.” Haw then paraphrases: tenant care about 60% of Pearson cost; about $100 a day less per diem and about $215,000 a year combined; overall health “at least as good,” with physical health maintained and mental health and social interactions improved; Canadian Council of Hospital Accreditation standards “met and exceeded in virtually all cases.” He adds that government “was not interested in measuring quality of life.” Those paraphrases are Haw’s, not a substitute for the evaluation.
4. A next project then in development would, Haw says, take the Creekview 202 concept further for seven ventilator-dependent Pearson residents. The inspected OCR uses both “Nobel House Cooperative” and “Noble Housing Co-op.” This archive does not equate that project with SCI BC history’s later “Stanley Noble Stronge Housing Cooperative” without a title-page match.

`source_type` is `near-primary`: a 1989 public talk by a CPA official about events a few years earlier, not the 1987 evaluation itself.
